title: The shroud
hook: plain white cloth, the same for the rich and the poor

segments.voice: Yesterday: washing the body, and your line, washed with care. Today, after the washing, the wrapping.

How was the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, dressed for his burial? 'A'ishah answers in Sahih al-Bukhari, and the answer is almost nothing. Three white sheets of Yemeni cotton. No shirt among them. No turban. The man his followers called the Messenger of Allah, wrapped in plain cloth, the way anyone could be. No embroidery, no rank, no sign of who he'd been. Just cloth, and the body inside it. Today's word is that cloth.
screen: `HOW WAS HE DRESSED FOR BURIAL?` → `THREE WHITE SHEETS.` → `NO SHIRT, NO TURBAN.`

segments.voice: The word is kafan, the shroud. A hadith in Abu Dawud gives the color, in paraphrase: wear white, for it's among the best of your clothes, and shroud your dead in it. So the custom is plain white cloth, wrapped around the washed body, the same whether the person owned a palace or a single room. Two more reports show what that can mean. In al-Bukhari, a man on pilgrimage was thrown from his camel at 'Arafah and killed, still wearing the two plain cloths of ihram. The Prophet said, in paraphrase: wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in his two garments. Don't perfume him, and don't cover his head, for he will be raised on the Day of Rising saying the pilgrim's call. His pilgrim's clothes became his shroud. And from Khabbab, also in al-Bukhari, the story of Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, killed at the battle of Uhud. All he left was one cloak. When they covered his head with it, his feet showed. When they covered his feet, his head showed. The Prophet told them to cover his head, and lay a sweet-smelling grass, idhkhir, over his feet. Not enough cloth, and still enough honor. Put those beside the three white sheets, and some readers hear the shroud saying something: that the things that separated people in life, the clothes, the labels, the bank balance, stay behind. What goes into the earth is wrapped in the same white.
screen: `KAFAN: THE SHROUD.` · `WEAR WHITE, SHROUD YOUR DEAD IN IT.` · `A PILGRIM IN HIS TWO CLOTHS.` · `ONE CLOAK, NOT ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Look down at what you're wearing, and think of the things you own that say something about you: a watch, a brand, a title on a badge, a car. Let each one fall away in your mind until there's only you, wrapped in something plain and white, and notice what's still there when the labels are gone. If you pray, rest in that plainness before Allah.
Kafan. The shroud: plain white cloth, the same for anyone, rich or poor. Today's word.
Your line: everyone in white. A palace or a single room, the same plain cloth. Day one thousand three hundred forty, done.

howItsDone: After the washing, Muslims wrap the body in a kafan of plain white cloth, kept simple whatever the person's wealth; a pilgrim who dies in ihram may be shrouded in the ihram garments.

chat.says: Why are Muslims buried in plain white? Don't rich people get something fancier?
options: No. The custom is plain white for rich and poor alike; even the Prophet's was.
Yes. Richer families add silk and embroidery to show the person's rank.
Only scholars and leaders get white; others are buried in their own clothes.
chat.meaning: Wear white and shroud your dead in it, a hadith says. 'A'ishah says the Prophet was wrapped in three white sheets, with no shirt or turban.

'Arafah.meaning: the plain near Makkah where pilgrims stand during Hajj

ihram.meaning: the pilgrim's sacred state, and its two plain cloths

Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr.meaning: a companion of the Prophet, killed at Uhud
